text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
American architect WILLIAM THORNTON, who created the Capitol in Washington, was born in 1759.
American co-founder of the freight-carrying company Wells Fargo, WILLIAM FARGO, was born in 1818.
West Australian mining promoter DORHAM DOOLETTE (known as "Dorrie"), was born in 1872.
The former Premier of Victoria and regarded as one of the most colourful figures in Australian politics, SIR HENRY BOLTE, was born in 1908.
American actor JAMES STEWART, whose many films include the Oscar-winning "The Philadelphia Story", was born in 1908.

English singer/songwriter JOE COCKER, who suffered from cerebral palsy as a child, was born in 1944. After starting his rock career in 1959 with 'The Caviliers', COCKER's solo version of the Beatles' number "I'll Cry Instead" was a flop, but he
later had more success with "With A Little Help From My Friends", "The Letter" and "You Are So Beautiful".
American singer and actress CHER (born CHERILYNN SARKASIAN LA PIERRE), who started out as a session-singer with PHIL SPECTOR, and is known for her sometimes raunchy costumes, was born in 1946.
British guitarist BRIAN NASH ("Frankie Goes To Hollywood") was born in 1963.
** EVENTS **
1303 : The Treaty of Paris restored Gascony to the
British in the Hundred Years War.
1498 : The explorer Vasco da Gama arrived at Calicut,
India, to complete his voyage around Africa.
1501 : The Portuguese discovered an island in the south
Atlantic on Ascension Day and named it Ascension Island.
1506 : Explorer CHRISTOPHER COLUMBUS died in Spain at the

age of 55, virtually broke and still believing he had reached Asia. He opened up the New World, but 14 years after his death, the Spanish Court still hadn't paid the royalties owed him for his discoveries.
1536 : The day after he beheaded his second wife ANNE
BOLEYN, KING HENRY VIII took the hand of JANE SEYMOUR in marriage.
1609 : The sonnets of WILLIAM SHAKESPEARE were published.
1736 : Englishman SAMUEL BALDWIN Esq. was buried at sea,
stipulating this wish in his will to prevent his wife from dancing on his grave, as she had threatened to do if she survived him!
1802 : France restored slavery and the slave trade in her
colonies.
1867 : Queen VICTORIA laid the foundation stone of the
Albert Hall in London.
1895 : Income Tax was declared unconstitutional in the
United States.
1902 : Cuba was handed over to a republican government
and the last U.S. troops left.
1910 : Thousands of people prepared for "the end of the

world" as Halley's Comet passed its closest to the Earth. Many people stayed home to meet the world's end with their families, while others bought "Comet Pills", that claimed to offer protection against the effects of the comet as it lit up the night sky.
1929 : The first airmail stamp was issued in Australia.
It showed a scene of gum trees and sheep.
1939 : PAN AM (Pan American Airways) began its first
commercial flights between the United States and Europe.
1941 : The Mediterranean island of Crete was invaded by
German paratroops.
1956 : The first hydrogen bomb to be dropped from the air
was exploded by the Americans over the Bikini Atoll in the Pacific.
1956 : British writer SIR MAX BEERBOHM died.
1961 : The "Orient Express" began its last journey from
Paris to Istanbul. Although dubbed "the king of trains and the train of kings", most kings by this time preferred flying.
1970 : The Beatles' film "Let It Be" premiered in London.
1980 : The Canadian province of Quebec voted against a
proposal to negotiate independence from Canada.
1989 : Martial Law was declared in Peking (Beijing) as
more than a million demonstrators gathered in support of pro-democracy campaigners on a hunger strike in Tiananmen Square.
1991 : The Soviet parliament approved in principle a law
which would allow citizens to travel aboard freely.
